title: Circles
prerequisites: Familiarity with the terms radius, diameter and circumference.
Angle sum property of a triangle and of a quadrilateral.
Idea of a perpendicular from a point to a line.

topics.title: Chords and Their Properties
topics.quick_summary: A perpendicular from the centre bisects a chord, equal chords are equidistant from the centre, and the longest chord of a circle is its diameter.
topics.real_life: To find the centre of a circular tabletop, draw two chords and their perpendicular bisectors — where they cross is the centre.

detailed.definition: A chord is a line segment joining two points on a circle. A diameter is a chord passing through the centre. An arc is a part of the circle, and a segment is the region between a chord and an arc.
detailed.key_idea: Every chord property comes from the isosceles triangle formed by the two radii to the chord's endpoints. Once that triangle is drawn, the results follow from congruence.
detailed.working_principle: The perpendicular from the centre to a chord bisects it, and conversely the line from the centre to the mid-point of a chord is perpendicular to it. Three non-collinear points determine exactly one circle.
applications: Equal chords of a circle subtend equal angles at the centre, and conversely.
Equal chords are equidistant from the centre, and conversely.
The longer chord is nearer to the centre.

points: The perpendicular from the centre to a chord bisects the chord.
The line joining the centre to the mid-point of a chord is perpendicular to it.
Equal chords are equidistant from the centre, and conversely.
The diameter is the longest chord of a circle.
One and only one circle passes through three non-collinear points.
mistakes: Assuming any line from the centre bisects a chord; it must be perpendicular to it.
Thinking a circle can be drawn through any three points; they must be non-collinear.
Saying the shorter chord is nearer the centre; it is the longer one.
topics.memory_hook: 'Perpendicular from the centre cuts the chord in half' — and 'longer chord, closer to the centre'.
topics.advanced: The perpendicular-bisector property is what makes trilateration possible. GPS locates a receiver by intersecting spheres, using exactly the three-points-determine-a-circle idea in three dimensions.

topics.title: Angles in a Circle and Cyclic Quadrilaterals
topics.quick_summary: The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference on the same arc, angles in the same segment are equal, and opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary.
topics.real_life: A camera placed anywhere on a certain arc sees a stage of fixed width at exactly the same angle — the equal-angles-in-the-same-segment property.

detailed.definition: A cyclic quadrilateral is a quadrilateral whose four vertices all lie on a circle. A segment is the region bounded by a chord and one of the arcs it cuts off.
detailed.key_idea: The central-angle theorem is the parent result. Angles in the same segment being equal, and the angle in a semicircle being 90°, are both immediate consequences of it.
detailed.working_principle: Because the angle at the centre standing on a diameter is 180°, the angle at the circumference on the same arc is 90° — which is why any angle in a semicircle is a right angle.
applications: The angle in a semicircle is always 90°.
Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral sum to 180°, and conversely.
The exterior angle of a cyclic quadrilateral equals the interior opposite angle.

points: Angle at the centre = 2 × angle at the circumference on the same arc.
Angles in the same segment of a circle are equal.
The angle in a semicircle is a right angle.
Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary, and conversely.
Equal arcs subtend equal angles at the centre.
mistakes: Halving instead of doubling when moving from the circumference to the centre.
Applying the equal-angles rule to angles in different segments.
Assuming every quadrilateral is cyclic; the vertices must be concyclic.
topics.memory_hook: 'Centre is double the circumference' — and 'a semicircle always gives a right angle'.
topics.advanced: The converse of the cyclic quadrilateral theorem is the standard test for concyclic points. Ptolemy's theorem extends it, relating the diagonals and sides of any cyclic quadrilateral in a single elegant equation.
